deep.reconstruction:
Context: the previous page (88) ends with a question that this page completes. On p. 88 Hilbert treated functions x(u1/u2, u3/u2) obtained by inverting quotients of solutions of a linear ODE, invariant under the monodromy group (compare Picard's functions).

(A) The question, spanning pp. 88-89, ends with a question mark: 'Is every finite group of linear transformations in arbitrarily many variables holoedrically isomorphic (= isomorphic) to a group of linear fractional substitutions in ONE variable, when these are taken congruent modulo a suitable module system consisting of entire integral functions (polynomials with integer coefficients)? (Congruence group with one variable.)'
Modern form: given a finite G ⊂ GL_n(C), is there an ideal M ⊂ Z[t1,...,tk] such that G embeds in PGL_2(Z[t]/M)? This is a question or programme, not a theorem. No argument is given.

(B) The theorem to be proved: 'If a finite group of transformations is given, one can always transform it (by a change of coordinates) so that the coefficients of the linear substitutions are rational functions of roots of unity.'
Modern form: for finite G ⊂ GL_n(C) there is P ∈ GL_n(C) with P G P^{-1} ⊂ GL_n(Q(ζ_N)) for some N. That is, every complex representation of a finite group is realizable over a cyclotomic field.

(C) A first proof strategy, struck through (both the line 'Man beweise zunächst folg.:' and the whole following paragraph):
Let the m substitutions have bilinear forms f1,...,fm (i.e. matrices A1,...,Am). Suppose parameters λ1..λm can be chosen so that the characteristic equation of λ1 f1 + ... + λm fm has n distinct roots. Then the group can be transformed into one whose substitution coefficients are rational functions [of the data].

Reconstruction of the intended idea (mine): a regular element of the group algebra lets one diagonalize. Its spectral idempotents e_ii are polynomials in that element. All other matrices are then fixed in that eigenbasis up to diagonal rescaling. The scaling can be normalized using traces of products, which are sums of roots of unity.

Why it was abandoned (my inference): the eigenvalues of a generic combination Σλ_i A_i are algebraic in λ, not cyclotomic, so this route does not give roots of unity.

The next page restarts with a different choice: take a single group element A, diagonal with distinct eigenvalues α1..αn. These are roots of unity since A^{|G|}=1. The eigen-lines are then determined, and the common scaling is fixed via the other substitutions (pencils and bundles of invariant linear forms).

Completion of that special case (mine): assume G is irreducible and contains A with distinct eigenvalues.
1. Then e_ii = Π_{j≠i}(A-α_j)/(α_i-α_j) ∈ Q(ζ)[A].
2. For each j choose g_j with (g_j)_{1j} ≠ 0 and rescale the basis so that (g_j)_{1j} = 1.
3. Then k_{j1} = tr(e_jj k e_11 g_j) ∈ Q(ζ) for every k ∈ G.
4. And h_{ij} k_{j1} = tr(e_11 g_i e_ii h e_jj k e_11) ∈ Q(ζ).
5. Choosing k with k_{j1} ≠ 0 shows h_{ij} ∈ Q(ζ).
So the special case is sound. The reducible case reduces to irreducible blocks.

The general theorem (no element with simple spectrum) is not covered by this method.
errors: The claim in (B) is announced as a theorem ('Beweis des Satzes'), but the method begun here and on the next page only handles groups containing an element (or a combination) with simple spectrum. The general statement is Brauer's theorem (1945/47) and needs much deeper tools (induction theorem). So any 'proof' along these lines would have a gap in general.

The crossed-out lemma (C) is imprecise. The eigenvalues of a generic λ-combination are not roots of unity, so its conclusion ('rationale Funktionen') cannot give cyclotomic coefficients. This is presumably why it was struck.

The question (A), if read as asking for an embedding into PGL_2 of a commutative quotient ring Z[t]/M, is very likely false. Over a field, finite subgroups of PGL_2 are cyclic, dihedral, A4, S4, A5, or PSL_2/PGL_2(F_q)-type (Dickson 1901). Over finite local rings the kernel to the residue field is a p-group. So e.g. A_7 does not occur, at least for finite or reduced quotient rings. Hilbert poses it only as a question (marked with '?').

results.what: Question whether every finite linear group is isomorphic to a group of linear fractional substitutions in one variable taken modulo a module system of integral polynomials ('Congruenzgruppe mit einer Veränderlichen')
results.modern_name: Embedding finite groups into PGL_2 over a quotient ring Z[t]/M; finite subgroups of PGL_2 (Dickson's classification)
results.usually_credited_to: Classification of finite subgroups of PGL_2(F_q): L.E. Dickson 1901 (building on Moore, Wiman). The question as posed appears to be Hilbert's own speculation.

results.what: Every finite group of linear substitutions is conjugate to one whose coefficients lie in a cyclotomic field
results.modern_name: Realizability of representations of finite groups over cyclotomic fields (Brauer's theorem, Schur's conjecture)
results.usually_credited_to: Conjectured/asked by Schur (c.1906-1909); proved by R. Brauer 1945 (over Q(ζ_e), e = exponent). The weaker algebraic-number version goes back to Frobenius/Burnside c.1900.

results.what: Method: diagonalize an element with distinct eigenvalues (roots of unity), then normalize the remaining matrices via the eigen-decomposition and trace relations
results.modern_name: Rationality via regular semisimple element / matrix units in the group algebra

deep.surprise_reason: Hilbert explicitly formulates, as a 'Satz' to be proved, that every finite linear group is conjugate into GL_n over a field generated by roots of unity. In print this question is associated with Schur and was only settled by Brauer in 1945. Here only special-case methods are sketched (and the first attempt is struck out), so it is an early formulation rather than a proof. The congruence-group question is speculative and likely false. Notable as a statement of intent, not a major result.

checkable.sympy: from sympy import Matrix, I, symbols, simplify; A=Matrix([[1,0],[0,-1]]); e11=(A-(-1)*Matrix.eye(2))/2; e22=(A-Matrix.eye(2))/(-2); simplify(e11+e22-Matrix.eye(2))==Matrix.zeros(2)
checkable.asserts: The spectral idempotents of a matrix with distinct eigenvalues are polynomials in it with coefficients rational in the eigenvalues, and they sum to the identity.

checkable.asserts: Trace identity tr(e11 g e11 h e22 k e11) = g11*h12*k21, used to show that entries are determined (hence cyclotomic) after normalization.

transcription_corrections: Line 2 ends with '?' followed by a stroke ('besteht.?'); it is a question completing the sentence begun on p. 88 ('Sind alle endlichen Gruppen ... ?'), not a stray mark.
The manuscript writes 'Substitionen' (sic) rather than 'Substitutionen' in the struck passage; harmless.

The whole paragraph from 'Man beweise zunächst folg.' to 'Funktionen sind.' is cancelled: the first line by a horizontal stroke, the rest by three large diagonal strokes. The transcription marks this correctly.
In 'λ_1 f_1 + ... + λ_m f_m' the subscript m on λ is written with an extra superscript 'm' above; it is simply λ_m.
